headline: From eMule to MoMA PS1: DJ Marfox and Lisbon's batida
standfirst: Born Marlon Silva in Lisbon in June 1988 to parents from São Tomé e Príncipe, DJ Marfox is credited with pioneering batida, the "ghetto sound of Lisbon" that came out of the city's housing estates. It fuses kuduro, kizomba, funaná and tarraxinha with house and techno.
body: DJ Marfox, born Marlon Silva in Lisbon in June 1988 to parents from São Tomé e Príncipe, is best known for pioneering batida, the "ghetto sound of Lisbon" that came out of the city's housing estates. It fuses African-influenced dance music such as kuduro, kizomba, funaná and tarraxinha with house and techno.

He has DJed as Marfox since 2002. The name joins "Marl" from Marlon with Star Fox, a Nintendo character he played as a teenager. In 2005 he founded DJs do Guetto with DJ Pausas and DJ Fofuxo. A year later the crew put DJs do Ghetto Vol. I, a 37-track digital compilation, on eMule. Príncipe Discos has since reissued it as a free download, and it is seen as the founding release of the ghetto sound of Lisbon.

His first solo album, Eu sei quem Eu Sou (I Know Who I Am), came out on Príncipe Discos in early 2011. Philip Sherburne described it as "an atomic field of taut drums, hiccupping yelps, zapping synths and pinprick details." Artist Unknown (Pollinaire, 2012) and Subliminar (Enchufada, 2013) followed.

In 2014 his Lucky Punch EP on Lit City Trax made Dazed's top ten albums for August. He played Red Bull Music Academy in New York, and on 30 August he played MoMA PS1's Warm Up series. Rolling Stone also named him among its "10 New Artists You Need to Know" that year. Cedar Pasori wrote that the PS1 appearance "reinforced the accelerating spread of Afro-Portuguese dance music around the world."

On 13 March 2015 Warp announced the Cargaa 1 EP for 7 April, with Marfox as its central figure. Three days later Revolução 2005–2008, a collection of tracks he made in his bedroom in those years, came out on CD and as a free download. One of his first international collaborations was a rework of tUnE-yArDs' "Water Fountain" featuring the Brazilian band Pearls Negras. His Chapa Quente EP includes "Tarraxo Everyday".

points.title: Where it started
points.text: In 2005 he founded DJs do Guetto with DJ Pausas and DJ Fofuxo. Their 37-track DJs do Ghetto Vol. I went up on eMule in 2006 and is seen as the founding release of the Lisbon ghetto sound.

points.title: Taking it global
points.text: In 2014 came Red Bull Music Academy in New York, Rolling Stone's "10 New Artists You Need to Know" and MoMA PS1's Warm Up on 30 August. In spring 2015 Warp's Cargaa 1 EP put him at its centre.

points.title: Start here
points.text: Eu sei quem Eu Sou (Príncipe Discos, 2011), which Philip Sherburne called "an atomic field of taut drums, hiccupping yelps, zapping synths and pinprick details." Then Subliminar (Enchufada, 2013), Revolução 2005–2008 and Chapa Quente.

headline: Tresor condemns Helsing AI military event at Kraftwerk
standfirst: Tresor has issued a statement condemning a military event held by Helsing AI at Kraftwerk Berlin.
body: Tresor has issued a statement condemning a military event held by Helsing AI at Kraftwerk Berlin.
The Berlin institution said such an event "has no place in the spaces our community has built".
The statement puts the club at odds with the use of a Berlin space closely linked to its community for an event tied to AI and the military.

headline: Arca, Justice and Fcukers land on the GTA VI album
standfirst: 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album' is out now and streaming, with Arca, Justice and Fcukers among the artists on the tracklist.
body: 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album' is out and available to listen to now. Arca, Justice and Fcukers are among the artists on it.
The LP comes right after the game's launch earlier this week. Grand Theft Auto VI had been a long time coming.
More artists appear on the album beyond those three. Arca, Justice and Fcukers are the names at the front of the coverage.
The release puts these artists, all familiar to people who follow electronic and club music, on the soundtrack album of one of the most anticipated games in years.

headline: CircoLoco gets its own radio station in GTA VI
standfirst: Grand Theft Auto VI launched worldwide this week, and its soundtrack includes CircoLoco Records Radio, hosted by Seth Troxler.
body: Grand Theft Auto VI came out worldwide this week, and club music has a big presence in it. One of its 22 radio stations is CircoLoco Records Radio. Seth Troxler hosts it, and it plays a batch of tracks that haven't been released yet.

The unreleased tracks are CHRIS STASSY's 'We On This Ride', DJ Tennis's 'Never Look Back' featuring Tomike, and 'I Feel Love' by Chloé Caillet & Myd. Also on the list: Mind Against's 'Let It Go', Carlita & Barker's 'Last Night', Troxler's own 'Bootlicker' and Rossi. & Demi's 'Deep N Sexy'. There are two remixes as well, Max Dean on Black Lounge's 'Bickering' and DJ Lag & Palms Trax on Rampa's 'The Church'. Released tracks by Michael Bibi, KETTAMA, PAWSA and Skream fill out the playlist.

There's more for club listeners. French duo Justice composed the game's original score. A hidden 23rd station called The Vault Radio reportedly unlocks once you find a poster inside The Vault, a fictional nightclub in downtown Vice City, and it plays the electronic mixes heard in that club. Gilles Peterson's Worldwide FM includes dubstep pioneer Mala, 4hero and the UK bass MC Magugu. Palms Trax and Burna Boy co-host AfroBank FM. Radio On-U takes its name from Adrian Sherwood's dub label On-U Sound. Flash FM includes Daft Punk and X-Press 2, and Robyn is one of its presenters.
The game also comes with a standalone 34-track album. Early reviews are overwhelmingly positive, and some critics already rank it among the best video games ever made.

The tie-in also carries over into real clubs. This weekend Miami's Club Space hosts a three-day takeover based on The Vault. Justice, Chris Lorenzo, Sammy Virji, Demi Riquísimo, DJ Tennis, Palms Trax, Seth Troxler and Skream are among the DJs playing.
Artists are already reacting. Max Dean and Black Lounge commented on DJ Mag's post that 'Bickering has been freed', and fans joked that the soundtrack will turn gamers into DJs.

points.title: A hidden club station
points.text: A 23rd station, The Vault Radio, reportedly unlocks when you find a poster inside The Vault, a fictional nightclub in downtown Vice City. It plays the club mixes heard inside the venue.

points.title: Selectors on the dial
points.text: Gilles Peterson hosts Worldwide FM, and Mala, 4hero and Magugu are on it. Palms Trax and Burna Boy front AfroBank FM. Radio On-U takes its name from Adrian Sherwood's dub label.

points.title: The Vault, for real
points.text: This weekend Miami's Club Space hosts a three-day takeover based on The Vault. Justice, Seth Troxler, DJ Tennis, Palms Trax, Skream, Sammy Virji and others are playing.

headline: Refuge NYC plans 63-hour NYE marathon with Tenaglia
standfirst: Refuge NYC will see in the New Year with ETERNIA, a dancefloor marathon that runs nonstop for 63 hours.
body: Refuge NYC is greeting the New Year with ETERNIA, a dancefloor marathon that will run for 63 hours without stopping.
Thirteen artists are booked across the event, drawn from house, techno and progressive music. Danny Tenaglia and Sasha lead the billing, and the rest of the lineup covers the same three genres.

The idea behind ETERNIA is an extended celebration, not a standard New Year's Eve party with a fixed closing time. With 63 hours to fill, the programme is built around one continuous dancefloor. The music keeps going from the countdown well into the days that follow.

The genre mix matters at that length. House, techno and progressive move at different energies and tempos, so booking across all three gives the run room to change mood over nearly three days instead of holding one pitch throughout.

Marathon formats like this ask something of the crowd as well as the DJs. Dancers can plan their own route through the weekend: arrive for a specific set, come back later, or try to stay as long as possible. Each person ends up with a different version of the party.

So far the published details are the format, the 63-hour length and the headline names. Set times, how the lineup is split across the run and ticketing information had not been included in the announcement.

headline: Korg phase8 gets free web app, firmware 1.3
standfirst: Korg's companion app for the phase8 acoustic synthesizer is now public. First shown at Superbooth in Berlin, it's free and runs in Chrome or Chromium browsers. Connect the phase8 over USB-C and it's ready to use.
body: Korg has released a free companion app for the phase8, its acoustic synthesizer, along with firmware version 1.3. The app was first shown at Superbooth in Berlin. It runs as a web application in Chrome and Chromium browsers: you plug the phase8 into a computer over USB-C and start working, with nothing to install.

The most obvious change is in the sequencer, which goes from 16 to 32 steps. The app also acts as a pattern editor and librarian. You can store patterns on your computer or on the instrument itself, and you can update the firmware from the same screen. Korg's Iarla Scaife in Berlin and Keisuke Nohara in Tokyo started the project, which adds on-screen tools for developing ideas so you're not working on the hardware alone.

This matters because the phase8 makes sound by physically exciting resonators, not with code. That has made it a talking point at a time when most music-making happens in software. Until now, the instrument offered limited ways to save and organise patterns. Being able to see a sequence on screen and keep a library of patterns makes it more practical in the studio and on stage.

Firmware 1.3 is available now. It fixes resonator behaviour that was sometimes unreliable, adds support for the companion app and improves sync and MIDI. Korg has published full release notes on its website.

Two other projects from Korg's Superbooth booth have no release plans yet: a set of custom bass resonators and a series of 3D-printed 'physical effects' by Hadrien Costrejean. Korg hasn't said whether either will be made more widely available.

points.title: What changes for you
points.text: phase8 owners can now write 32-step patterns, see their sequences on screen and back up their work to a computer. It costs nothing and needs only a browser and a USB-C cable.

points.title: Why update to 1.3
points.text: Firmware 1.3 fixes the resonators that sometimes behaved unpredictably and improves sync and MIDI. It's also required to use the new companion app.

points.title: Still unreleased
points.text: At Superbooth, Korg also showed custom bass resonators and 3D-printed 'physical effects' by Hadrien Costrejean. There's no word yet on whether either will get a wider release.

headline: Serato opens SoundSpace artist hub in Los Angeles
standfirst: Serato has opened SoundSpace, a 4,500-square-foot headquarters for DJs, producers and artists in Los Angeles' Arts District. It will host workshops and live showcases, and visiting artists can use the company's full product suite.
body: Serato has opened SoundSpace, a new headquarters for DJs, producers and artists in the Arts District of Los Angeles. The 4,500-square-foot site will host workshops and live showcases. Visiting artists get hands-on access to the company's full range of products.

The building has three main areas: a production studio, a tech library and a dedicated DJ space. The audio was designed by NNNN and OJAS. The DJ setup is built around two custom ON8 loudspeakers from the pair, and these are the first to use wide-dispersion multisectoral horns. It is also NNNN's first commercial installation in Los Angeles.

In the production studio, producers will work on NNNN's U15 nearfield monitoring system, which hasn't been released yet. The tech library holds a selection of Serato controllers and mixers for artists to try. Serato's Artist Relations team, made up of DJs, producers and audio engineers, will be on site to give technical support.
The space had its soft launch with DJ sets from The Alchemist, Novena Carmel and Jared Jackson.
Upcoming events include a private listening party with producer Dahi and workshops with Beatport, Kittens and Duckworld.

For working DJs and producers, the appeal is clear. SoundSpace mixes a showroom, a studio and a venue, with a sound system built specifically for the room and a monitoring setup that isn't available anywhere else yet.

points.title: The sound system
points.text: The DJ area runs two custom OJAS and NNNN ON8 loudspeakers, the first to use wide-dispersion multisectoral horns. It is also NNNN's first commercial installation in Los Angeles.

points.title: Inside the studio
points.text: The production studio uses NNNN's U15 nearfield monitoring system, which hasn't been released yet. The tech library holds a selection of Serato controllers and mixers.

points.title: What's next
points.text: Coming up are a private listening party with producer Dahi and workshops with Beatport, Kittens and Duckworld. Serato's Artist Relations team will give technical support on site.

headline: Sven Väth and Roman Flügel open Time Warp Records
standfirst: After more than three decades of throwing parties, Time Warp has started its own record label.
body: Time Warp has launched its own record label. The first release, catalogue number TWR001, is 'Rings of Light', a collaboration between Sven Väth and Roman Flügel.
The label comes after more than three decades of Time Warp events. Snippets of the record are available on Time Warp's official channel, so you can hear a preview before getting the full release.

Starting a catalogue at 001 shows the label has plans beyond a single record. Opening with a joint credit from Väth and Flügel ties the label's first release to two artists whose careers have both run alongside the party series. For now the material confirms only the title, the artists and the catalogue number. Nothing has been announced about formats, a tracklist, or what comes after TWR001.

Plenty of club and festival brands have turned their name into a label, using the reputation they built on the dancefloor to release music under their own banner. Time Warp is now doing the same, though with three decades of parties behind it. How the label develops will depend on who it signs next and whether it sticks with established names or makes space for newer producers.
For now, the 'Rings of Light' snippets are the first sound of the new label. HARDMAG will report details on the full release, formats and future catalogue numbers once they are confirmed.

headline: Kraftwerk Berlin apologises for hosting Helsing event
standfirst: Kraftwerk, the Berlin venue, has apologised for hosting an exhibition for Helsing, a company that makes AI weapons.
body: Kraftwerk, the Berlin venue, has apologised for hosting an exhibition for Helsing, a company that makes AI weapons.

Mixmag reported the story and said the venue was fitted out to look like a "military command post" for the event. Those are the only details of the set-up given so far. The report does not include the wording of Kraftwerk's apology, the date of the exhibition or what was on show.

The apology matters beyond one booking. Berlin's electronic music community sees its spaces as more than rooms for hire. Many people in the scene treat them as places with shared values, and they watch closely who uses them when the music stops. Seeing a venue linked to the city's club and arts world dressed as a military operations room for a weapons maker is bound to provoke a reaction.

The story also touches a debate that keeps growing: how artificial intelligence is moving from studios and streaming platforms into far less benign areas. HARDMAG follows AI in music closely, from production tools to rights and royalties. This case is a reminder that the same technology also powers businesses that many artists and ravers would not want to be associated with.

The questions left open are practical ones that every venue faces with private and corporate hire. Who decides which clients are acceptable? Is there any vetting before a contract is signed? And what does an apology change for future bookings?
HARDMAG will update this story if Kraftwerk or Helsing release more details about the event or the venue's response.

headline: DJ Ride wins DMC World Open title at London's KOKO
standfirst: DJ Ride has won the Open category at the 41st DMC World DJ Championships, held on Saturday at KOKO in London. It is his first DMC world title.
body: DJ Ride has won the Open category at the DMC World DJ Championships. He took the title on Saturday at KOKO in London, where the competition held its 41st edition, and it is his first DMC world title.

DMC has run since 1985 and is often called the Olympics of DJing. It is the best-known contest in turntablist culture, with a reputation for technical difficulty and inventive routines. Open competitors have to combine technique, musicality and creativity while building a set that works for the audience, all within 12 minutes.

Ride got to London by winning the Open category at DMC Iberia, held in Vigo in August. In a thank-you post on Instagram, he said he had wanted to be DMC world champion, and to earn the gold record and jacket, since the first time he touched a turntable. He described going from last place to first after many attempts and years of hard work. He also said part of his set was a love letter to British music, which he has been listening to since childhood, and added that he would have said more if the round weren't capped at 12 minutes.

The win adds to an already strong competition record. Ride holds four world titles from the International DJ Association (IDA). Two came in 2011 and 2016 as part of Beatbombers, his duo with Stereossauro. The other two were individual IDA titles in the Show and Technical categories in 2023.

Stereossauro won the DMC Open in 2024, so both halves of Beatbombers have now won the category. Ride's career spans hip-hop, electronic music and new approaches to turntablism, and this title makes him one of the leading competition DJs in the world.

points.title: From last to first
points.text: Ride says he wanted the DMC gold record and jacket from the first time he touched a turntable. He describes going from last place to first after years of attempts.

points.title: Fifth world title
points.text: He already holds four IDA world titles: two with Beatbombers in 2011 and 2016, plus individual Show and Technical titles in 2023.

points.title: A Beatbombers double
points.text: His Beatbombers partner Stereossauro won the DMC Open in 2024, so both members of the duo have now taken the category.

headline: Craig Richards plays his first all-night set at fabric
standfirst: Craig Richards will play open to close at fabric on Saturday, January 16th, 2027. It will be the first time in his 27-year residency at the London club that he plays the whole night alone.
body: Craig Richards is set to play his first open-to-close set at fabric on Saturday, January 16th, 2027. That's a first in the 27 years he has held a residency at the London club.

Richards has been a resident since fabric opened its doors in 1999. Through his selections and programming, he has had a central hand in shaping the club's musical identity over that time. He has played plenty of long sets in different rooms and formats, but he has never covered an entire night alone, from the moment the doors open until closing.
He's aware of how unusual that is. "After twenty-seven years and nearly eight hundred occasions, it's strange to think that I have never played alone for the duration of the night," Richards says.

On the night, Richards alone will control the music in Room One from start to finish. It's a new format for one of fabric's longest-serving residents, and it puts one DJ in charge of how the whole night is shaped and paced.

For a club whose identity is tied so closely to its residents, the date is a milestone for both the DJ and the venue. For anyone who has followed Richards' sets at fabric over the years, it's a rare chance to hear him play a full night in the room he helped define.

headline: Deezer study: 72% of listeners want AI music transparency
standfirst: In a new survey from Deezer, 72% of music streaming users said they want more transparency about AI-generated music on streaming platforms.
body: Most music streaming users want platforms to be clearer about AI-generated music. In a survey from Deezer, 72% of respondents said they want more transparency about AI music on streaming services.

The survey also found that many listeners don't realise they're already hearing it. Almost three-quarters of respondents believed their playlists had no AI-generated music, but 57% of respondents did have AI tracks on them.

That gap is the main finding. Most listeners say they care where their music comes from, but many can't tell when a track was made by AI. When AI music can sit on a playlist without anyone noticing, a label or tag may be the only way listeners can know what they're hearing.

This matters for the electronic music community. Producers, labels and DJs who build their work around streaming are now competing with AI-generated tracks that listeners often can't spot. Clear labelling would let listeners choose for themselves and would make it easier to see which music came from a human artist.

The figures come from Deezer's own survey, as reported by Mixmag. In short, most of the listeners surveyed want to know when music was made by AI, and many of them are already hearing it without knowing.

points.title: The perception gap
points.text: Almost three-quarters of respondents believed they had no AI tracks on their playlists. In fact, 57% did. Many listeners can't tell when they're hearing AI music.

points.title: Why it matters
points.text: Human producers are competing for the same playlist spots as AI tracks that listeners often can't spot. Most users surveyed say they want that made visible.

points.title: The ask
points.text: 72% of the streaming users surveyed want platforms to be more transparent about AI-generated music.

headline: Spotify vows to protect artists from misattributed AI tracks
standfirst: Spotify says it will "protect" artists from AI-generated tracks that are wrongly attributed to them, Mixmag reports.
body: Spotify says it will "protect" artists from AI-generated tracks that are misattributed to them, according to a report from Mixmag. The streaming giant is not stepping back from AI, though. AI use is still allowed on the platform, and Spotify is preparing to launch an AI remix service in 2027.

Those two moves sum up where the biggest streaming service now stands on machine-made music. It is promising artists some protection when their names are attached to AI tracks they had nothing to do with. At the same time, it is keeping its doors open to AI content and building its own AI product.

For DJs and producers in electronic music, misattribution is not an abstract worry. An artist's name on a streaming profile drives discovery, bookings and royalties, so a track wrongly credited to that name hits all three. Spotify's pledge is a public acknowledgement that the problem exists on its platform.

The planned remix service matters just as much. Remixing has long been one of the core crafts of club music. A platform-built AI tool for it raises clear questions for the producers whose work feeds that culture: who gets credited, who gets paid, and how much control original artists will have.
The report doesn't say how Spotify will carry out its protection pledge or how the 2027 remix service will work. HARDMAG will follow both as more details come out.

headline: Berlin Atonal condemns Kraftwerk over AI military event
standfirst: Berlin Atonal has publicly said it "strongly condemns" Kraftwerk, the former power station in Mitte that has long been its home, after the venue hosted an exhibition for an AI military firm.
body: Berlin Atonal has said it "strongly condemns" Kraftwerk, the former power station in Berlin's Mitte district where the festival is staged. The criticism follows the venue's decision to host an exhibition for an AI military firm.
In its statement, the festival said it "should not be housed in a space that goes against its values". That is unusually direct language from an event about the building it is identified with.
Even so, Atonal will return to Kraftwerk for its next edition. Based on what has been reported, the festival is objecting to the venue's choice of client without leaving the building.

For the club and festival community, the episode raises a question beyond Berlin. Large industrial venues often take on corporate and private bookings alongside cultural programming. Artists and promoters cannot always choose who else uses the spaces where their events take place.

The AI connection makes the story more pointed. AI is already changing how music is made and distributed, and its use in military technology is now an issue for one of electronic music's most closely watched festivals.
The festival's next edition at the former Mitte power station will be the first since the dispute.

points.title: Why it matters
points.text: It is rare for a festival to publicly criticise its own venue. The dispute links AI, the military and the spaces where electronic music happens.

points.title: The contradiction
points.text: Atonal says the festival should not be housed in a space that goes against its values. It is still returning to Kraftwerk for its next edition.

points.title: What to watch
points.text: The festival's next edition at the former Mitte power station will be the first since the dispute.

headline: Vilnius Nights: four clubs, one €10 ticket
standfirst: In 2026, Vilnius Days, the Lithuanian capital's 33-year-old street festival, extended into Vilnius Nights for the first time. Four nightclubs stayed open until 6AM, and one €10 ticket got you into all of them.
body: In 2026, Vilnius Days, the Lithuanian capital's 33-year-old street festival, extended into Vilnius Nights for the first time. Four nightclubs stayed open until 6AM, and one €10 ticket got you into all of them.

The Vilnius Night Office ran the initiative. The city municipality set up this public institution in 2023. It gives venues financial aid, offers staff training and mental health support, and runs harm reduction campaigns.
The event came months after Opium Club, open since 2009, closed in February. Mixmag also visited Draugų Vardai, an art and music space with a custom-built soundsystem.

headline: Tourism boom squeezes Reykjavík's music venues
standfirst: Tourism-driven gentrification is pushing Reykjavík's music venues out to make way for hotels and restaurants, artists and industry figures told Mixmag during Iceland Airwaves.
body: Tourism-driven gentrification is pushing Reykjavík's music venues out to make way for hotels and restaurants, artists and industry figures told Mixmag during Iceland Airwaves.

The festival's 27th edition ran across just seven spaces, including punk bar Lemmy, the Kolaport market hall, an independent church and City Hall. Producer Ida Juhl, aka knackered, says DIY crews host parties in bars they don't own: "pull up, build the stage and build the sound."
A newly formed Reykjavík Nighttime Industries Advocacy Group is now working to support and protect the city's venues.

headline: Mamdani names Eric Thor NYC nightlife director
standfirst: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has named Eric Thor Executive Director of the city's Office of Nightlife. Mamdani announced the appointment on Friday, November 13.
body: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has named Eric Thor Executive Director of the city's Office of Nightlife. Mamdani announced the appointment on Friday, November 13.

Thor was born in Queens and was previously lead developer at LaborLab, an organisation that supports unionisation. He will meet workers, business owners and community members across all five boroughs to shape the office's priorities, with a focus on working conditions and licensing.
“Nightlife is for everyone, from clubs to queer spaces to immigrant-run venues,” Thor said.

headline: Detroit to celebrate the life of Juan Atkins
standfirst: The family of Juan Atkins will host a public celebration of the electronic music pioneer's life and legacy on Sunday, November 22nd, at The Lincoln Factory in Detroit.
body: The family of Juan Atkins will host a public celebration of the electronic music pioneer's life and legacy on Sunday, November 22nd, at The Lincoln Factory in Detroit.
The 12-hour gathering is open to family, friends, fans and fellow artists. In its Instagram announcement, the family wrote: "All are welcome. Please celebrate his life and work with us."
Atkins died on November 1st in Mexico City, aged 64. His foundational role in Detroit techno helped establish a musical language that has shaped generations of producers and DJs worldwide.
